title: If You Press a Pedal With Your Foot...
sources: HowStuffWorks 'How Brakes Work' (science.howstuffworks.com/brake.htm) / Jalopnik 'Here's How Your Foot Is Able To Bring A 4,000 Pound Car To A Halt': leverage plus hydraulics multiply pedal force

Wikipedia 'Hydraulic brake' / HowStuffWorks 'Hydraulic machines: the basic idea' / MSU College Physics 'Pascal's principle' / YourMechanic 'How does brake fluid work': brake fluid is nearly incompressible; pressure from the master cylinder is sent equally to all wheels and larger caliper pistons multiply the force
Wikipedia 'Power brake' / HowStuffWorks 'How Power Brakes Work': the vacuum booster uses engine vacuum to add force to the pedal push
Wikipedia 'Brake' / FenderBender 'The physics of braking': friction brakes turn the car's kinetic energy into heat
Wikipedia 'Brake fade' / Brake & Front End 'Brake Fade (Pads Overheat)': overheated brakes lose grip (fade)
US patents 'Ventilated brake rotor' / 'Internally-ventilated brake disks with improved cooling' / AA1Car 'Brake rotor': vented discs have internal vanes that pump cooling air

24h-lemans.com 'Why do brakes glow red during the 24 Hours of Le Mans?' / FlowRacers 'How Hot Do F1 Brakes Get?' / IMSA 'Lexus tech talk: brakes': race brake discs glow red at well over 1,000 degrees F (F1 discs ~1,000 C)

HowStuffWorks 'How Anti-Lock Brakes Work' / YourMechanic 'How Anti-Lock Brakes Work' / Consumer Guide 'What are anti-lock brakes?': locked wheels skid and can't steer; ABS pulses the brakes up to about 15 times per second so the driver keeps steering

lines.text: If you press a pedal with your foot, a two-ton car stops.
lines.caps: If you press a pedal | with your foot, | a 2-ton car stops.

lines.text: But your foot alone isn't strong enough to stop two tons.
lines.caps: But your foot alone | isn't strong enough | to stop 2 tons.

lines.text: So, the pedal pushes a piston into brake fluid, which can't be squeezed.
lines.caps: So, the pedal pushes a piston | into brake fluid, | which can't be squeezed.

lines.text: That fluid carries the push to all four wheels, and makes it bigger.
lines.caps: That fluid carries the push | to all 4 wheels, | and makes it bigger.

lines.text: And a booster uses engine vacuum to push even harder.
lines.caps: And a booster | uses engine vacuum | to push even harder.

lines.text: At each wheel, a caliper squeezes pads onto a spinning steel disc.
lines.caps: At each wheel, | a caliper squeezes pads | onto a spinning steel disc.

lines.text: Friction turns the car's motion into heat.
lines.caps: Friction turns | the car's motion | into heat.

lines.text: But hot brakes grip less. It's called brake fade.
lines.caps: But hot brakes | grip less. | It's called brake fade.

lines.text: So, the discs have air vanes inside, like a fan, to cool them down.
lines.caps: So, the discs | have air vanes inside, | like a fan, | to cool them down.

lines.text: On race cars, they still glow red hot, at over a thousand degrees.
lines.caps: On race cars, | they still glow red hot, | at over 1,000 degrees.

lines.text: But squeeze too hard, and the wheels lock up, and the car slides.
lines.caps: But squeeze too hard, | and the wheels lock up, | and the car slides.

lines.text: So, ABS pumps the brakes up to fifteen times a second, so you can still steer.
lines.caps: So, ABS pumps the brakes | up to 15 times a second, | so you can still steer.

lines.text: You see, brakes don't stop your car. They turn its speed into heat.
lines.caps: You see, brakes | don't stop your car. | They turn its speed | into heat.

lines.text: That's why your wheels feel hot after a long drive down a mountain.
lines.caps: That's why your wheels | feel hot after a long drive | down a mountain.
